messages:
carmen: Ran perfetto + nsys on the nightly inference run for gpt-medium-8k (q4f16). Seeing intermittent 300-600ms stalls during the first few token steps. Trace points to compile activity right before those stalls.

jeet: Can you paste the compact nsys flame or a short timeline extract? Curious if it shows a "triton compile"/"jit_compile" long span or CPU-side blocking.

carmen: Small excerpt from the timeline and kernel log:
```
[GPU] triton::compile_kernel(shape=(1,64), name=attention_fwd)   0.54s  <-- compile
[GPU] triton_kernel_attention_fwd                             0.12s  <-- first run
[GPU] generic_gemm                                             0.003s
Kernel cache stats: total_signatures=2000, cache_miss=22%, cache_insert=14%, avg_compile=0.42s
```
Cache churn looks high. Many unique shapes from variable prefixes.

sophie: That matches a warmup + per-shape compile story. If your batching heuristic is producing a lot of different (batch, seq_len) signatures we can easily blow the cache and pay compile cost often. What batching rules were you using?

carmen: Dynamic batching up to 32, pad-to-nearest=8. Problem: lots of short prompts with varied prefixes -> shapes like (1,13),(1,21),(1,29) etc.

jeet: Two quick experiments: 1) enable persistent kernel cache with REDWOOD_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR and reuse across runs, 2) try coalescing shapes (pad-to-64) to reduce unique signatures. If compile is ~400-600ms it's going to dominate tail latency for cold signatures.

perf-bot: [automated] tagged with perf, created PERF-2453 for follow-up and triage.

sophie: Also instrument NVTX around the compile path ("triton::compile") and emit a lightweight kernel_cache.log with records like: key,count,compile_time. That will help correlate CPU stall spans in perfetto with GPU compile events. For repro, run nsys with cpu sampling: `nsys profile -o run --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=cpu python bench_infer.py`.

carmen: Repro command I used:
```
nsys profile -o nightly_gpt8k --trace=nvtx,cuda python infra/bench_infer.py --model gpt-medium-8k --batching dynamic --pad 8
```
I'll re-run with REDWOOD_KERNEL_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/rwc and pad-to-64 as suggested and attach the kernel_cache.log.

jeet: If persistent cache + coalescing doesn't get cache_miss < 10%, we should consider: a) throttling/serializing first-time compiles to avoid token-blocking, b) precompiling hot shapes at model load (sampling common seq_len distribution), c) adding a small LRU for compile artifacts with eviction tuned to workload.

sophie: Agreed. Also check if the runtime falls back to a generic (slower) kernel when compile fails or times out — that fallback could mask compiles but still add latency. NVTX + nsys will show fallback patterns.

carmen: Sounds good — I'll run both experiments tomorrow (persistent cache + pad-to-64) and post the new nsys perfetto link + kernel_cache.log. If we still see >10% misses we'll open a small spike to prototype precompile and compile-throttle. Thanks :thumbsup:
